title: Spot a rolling boil
summary: Learn the difference between a simmer and a proper rolling boil for pasta.
score_on: water at a full rolling boil
lid used to speed it up
notes: Hot water: keep the pan handle turned in and never lean over the pan.

steps.instruction: Half fill a pan with water, put the lid on and turn the heat to high. Turn the handle inwards, away from the edge.
looks_wrong: handle sticking out over the edge
steps.done_when: The pan is heating with the lid on.

steps.instruction: Watch it change: tiny bubbles on the bottom (not yet), then small bubbles rising (a simmer), then big bubbles breaking all over the surface (a rolling boil).
looks_right: big bubbles breaking across the whole surface
looks_wrong: only small bubbles on the bottom
gentle simmer at the edges only
steps.done_when: The water is at a rolling boil that doesn't stop when you stir it.

steps.instruction: Turn the heat down until it just simmers: small, steady bubbles. That's the difference.
looks_right: small, steady bubbles after turning down
steps.done_when: You've seen a rolling boil and a simmer.
